gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the Jabra speakerphone that connects to a laptop by Bluetooth is the Speak2 75 bought in a variant with a Jabra Link USB-A or USB-C adapter, because the Speak2 55 it recommended for Zoom and Teams connects to a computer only by its cable and its Bluetooth works with phones and tablets only.
standout_why: I compared against the cited jabra.com Speak2 55 overview (result 1), the uncited Jabra Speak2 55 buy page (result 4), and the cited bose.com SoundLink Flex (2nd Gen) page (result 7). The cited Jabra 55 page already says the computer connection is 'via cable only', that Bluetooth is 'for smartphone/tablet only', and that the 55 'comes without USB Bluetooth adapter'. So rivals have the limit, but ChatGPT's card still said 'USB and Bluetooth connectivity' without that warning. None of the results covers the Speak2 75 or its adapter variants. None names which Bose speakers can pair with the Flex (2nd Gen) in Party or Stereo mode; the cited bose.com page says only 'compatible speakers'.
decides: For a shopper who wants a wireless speakerphone for laptop calls, the Speak2 55 does not do that job. The pick moves to the Speak2 75 in a variant that includes the Jabra Link adapter, not the variant without one. If the 55's cable to the computer is fine, the 55 still works, and the shopper should choose the UC variant unless they use Teams. For the Bose Flex (2nd Gen), the finding only adds a pairing note: Party mode works with the Flex (2nd Gen), Max, Micro (2nd Gen) and Plus, and Stereo mode needs two of the same model.

findings.label: How it connects to a computer
findings.value: By cable only (one cable with both USB-C and USB-A ends). Bluetooth is for smartphones and tablets only.
findings.note: FAQ: 'You can connect your speakerphone to both your computer (connection via cable only) and your smartphone or tablet (via Bluetooth) at the same time.' Also: 'Speak2 55 comes with both USB A and USB C connectors on the same cable.'

findings.label: USB Bluetooth adapter in the box
findings.note: FAQ: 'No. Speak2 55 comes without USB Bluetooth adapter.' Box contents listed as speakerphone, carry pouch, safety information and warranty. The page does not say whether a separately bought Jabra Link adapter works with the 55.

findings.label: Bluetooth version, range and connections
findings.value: Bluetooth 5.1, up to 30 m (98 ft), up to 8 paired devices, 2 connected at once
findings.note: Taken from the maker's spec block and FAQ.

findings.label: Meeting platforms and variants
findings.value: Microsoft Teams (Teams-certified variant only), Google Meet, Amazon Chime, Google Fast Pair, works with Chromebook. Jabra recommends the standard UC variant for anyone not on Teams.
findings.note: The Teams variant adds a dedicated Teams button and automatic default-device selection. Jabra also says: 'Remote call control functionality is dependent on the video or audio conferencing software being used.'

findings.label: Wireless connection to a computer
findings.value: Through a Jabra Link Bluetooth adapter, sold in USB-A or USB-C variants. There is also a variant with no adapter. The speaker's own Bluetooth is for smartphones and tablets only.
findings.note: FAQ: 'You can choose between either USB-A or USB-C Bluetooth adapter... There is also a variant without one included.' It also says you can connect to your computer 'with the supplied Jabra Link 380 Bluetooth adapter', marked '*Variant dependent'. The spec line reads 'USB C or USB A, Bluetooth (for smartphone/tablet only)'. Jabra's page names the adapter inconsistently: the FAQ says Link 380, but the box contents say 'Link 390 Bluetooth adapter (variant dependent)'.

findings.label: Bluetooth version, range and connections
findings.value: Bluetooth 5.2, up to 30 m (98 ft), up to 8 paired devices, 2 connected at once
findings.note: Taken from the maker's spec block. It also comes in Teams-certified and standard UC variants.

findings.label: Speakers it can link with in Party and Stereo mode
findings.value: SoundLink Flex (2nd Gen), SoundLink Max, SoundLink Micro (2nd Gen), SoundLink Plus. Stereo mode works only between two speakers of the same model.
findings.source_title: Difficulty using Party or Stereo modes | Bose SoundLink Flex Portable Speaker (2nd Gen) (Bose support, Japan site)
findings.note: This is Bose's own support article. It is on the Japanese site, but the speaker list is in English. Both speakers need the Speaker Link shortcut turned on, and Bose says to install any available updates. The first-generation Flex is not on the list. The US product page says only 'compatible speakers'.

findings.label: Microphone and call controls
findings.value: Built-in microphone. Press play/pause to answer a call; double-press to decline or end it.
findings.source_title: SoundLink Flex Portable Speaker (2nd Gen) | Bose
findings.note: The spec sheet lists 'Built-in Microphone' and the comparison table marks Microphone 'Yes'. Bose's product page also describes multipoint: two source devices connected at once.

findings.label: Price, Black (bose.com US)
findings.source_title: Shop SoundLink Flex Bluetooth Speaker (2nd Gen) | Bose
findings.note: No sale price shown. The Blue Dusk Plaid Holiday Limited Edition is $199.00 on the cited page. The page also states Bluetooth 5.3 with a range of about 30 ft.

findings.label: Microphone, Bluetooth and price (marshall.com US)
findings.value: Built-in mic for hands-free calls; Bluetooth 5.3 LE; multipoint; $179.99
findings.note: Marshall says it is 'ready for LE Audio once there are source devices on the market'. Auracast is described as coming later, not available now. The page did not mention Stack Mode or codecs.
